purpose: verifier-profile-research.json located WHICH top-level step of ZKVerifier::verify dominates cost (94-97% in the second step, wrapped_channel.finish()) using the pinned verifier's own tracing::info_span! instrumentation, but stated that step 'cannot be decomposed further without new spans in pinned source' -- which this project does not add, to avoid modifying pinned/vendored dependency code. This file closes that gap with a different, span-free technique: a pure-userspace, signal-based sampling profiler, which needs no new spans and touches no pinned source, to get real function-level attribution inside that step.
method: Added the `pprof` crate (v0.15.0, SIGPROF-based signal sampling, no perf_event_open, no system package install, no sudo) as a dependency of the existing research tool via `cargo add pprof --features flamegraph,frame-pointer`, in a new binary `src/bin/pprof_profile.rs` alongside the existing tracing-span binary (unmodified). Initial runs captured zero resolved stack frames per sample; debugging found pprof's frame-pointer unwinder needs the binary actually built with forced frame pointers, which a scoped `.cargo/config.toml` (`rustflags = ["-C", "force-frame-pointers=yes"]`, applying only to this tool directory) supplies without touching any other crate's build settings. Two passes were then run against the same pinned, SHA256-verified fixtures used throughout this project's Binius64 evidence: a module-level pass (3 runs of 300 verify_preprocessed_detailed iterations at 2000 Hz, ~8000 samples per run) and one function-level pass (400 iterations at 1000 Hz, 3181 samples) for representative per-function detail.

module_level_breakdown_pct_of_samples_3_.note: Grouped by the first two '::'-path segments of each sample's leaf (innermost) resolved frame. Ranges are the min-max across the 3 independent runs (~8000 samples each), not a single point estimate, to show sampling variance honestly.

function_level_breakdown_pct_of_samples_.note: eq_ind_partial_eval_scalars is called FROM evaluate_segment_wiring_mle (confirmed by reading wiring.rs); it is not an independent cost center, so the wiring module's effective total is closer to 44.01+22.01+15.09+5.44 = ~86.6% of this run's samples, not just the 71% module-level figure (which groups by leaf frame's own module, undercounting a shared helper's module if it were attributed to binius_math instead -- shown here unmerged for transparency).

why_wiring_dominates.structurally_expected_cost: Confirmed directly against crates/spartan-verifier/src/lib.rs:195-237: two eval_transparent closures (wiring.rs) are built, one per WitnessSegment (Precommit, Private), both sharing one cached r_x_tensor, and invoked via channel.verify_oracle_relations(...). Each resulting evaluate_segment_wiring_mle call (wiring.rs) loops over every multiplication constraint in the real, padded constraint system (sized by the actual SHA-512/clamp/scalar-mult seed-recovery relation's full gate count) and, per constraint, sums over each of the 3 operands' (a, b, c) wire lists. This is linear in (constraint count x fan-in per operand) field-arithmetic work -- the structurally expected cost of evaluating a real circuit's wiring MLE at verification time, not an implementation defect.
why_wiring_dominates.candidate_inefficiency_unconfirmed: evaluate_segment_wiring_mle's own doc comment states r_x_tensor is accepted as a parameter specifically 'to avoid redundant computation when evaluating multiple segments with the same r_x' -- and lib.rs:224-237 does pass the identical r_x_tensor to both the Precommit and Private calls. There is no equivalent caching for the r_y side: the function recomputes `eq_ind_partial_eval_scalars(r_y)` from scratch on every call (wiring.rs). Whether r_y is actually identical across the Precommit and Private calls in verify_oracle_relations (which would make this a real, confirmable redundant computation) was not measured here and is not assumed; stated as a candidate worth a future, narrowly-scoped measurement, not a confirmed bug or a proposed fix.

conclusion: This identifies WHERE the dominant verification cost is, at function granularity, going beyond verifier-profile-research.json's step-level result. It does not close F-01: it does not reduce CPU cost, does not reduce SDK code size, and does not change A-01 or F-01's status in SECURITY_REVIEW.md's findings table. Actually modifying evaluate_segment_wiring_mle or evaluate_wiring_mle_public's behavior would mean either forking the pinned binius-spartan-verifier/binius-math crates under a new, separately-maintained name (a substantial, security-sensitive undertaking needing its own independent review before any such change could be trusted) or proposing a change upstream to the real IrreducibleOSS/binius64 project (an external-visibility action). Neither was attempted; this round deliberately stops at diagnosis and hands the optimization question to a future, explicitly-scoped engineering task or to the eventual independent cryptographic reviewer already scoped in BINIUS_A01_REVIEW_SCOPE.md.
scope_and_limits: Native, single-threaded, release-build sampling-profiler proxy; not a Soroban metered-instruction count.

Sampling-based, not exhaustive: percentages are statistical estimates. The module-level breakdown is reported as a 3-run range, not a single average, to show real run-to-run variance rather than hide it.
Does not modify, re-time, or add instrumentation to pinned/vendored source; all measurement happens from this project's own, separate research-tool code calling the existing public API from outside.
The r_y-caching observation under why_wiring_dominates is an unconfirmed candidate, not a verified defect or a recommended code change.
Confirms the existing canonical fixture is accepted in every run; performs no new cryptographic claim and changes no account, asset, or authorization state.
